memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So the Lord brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror and with signs and wonders. He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey." — Deut 26:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God heard, and then God acted. He did not merely feel sorry for His people — He rescued them with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. The signs and wonders in Egypt, the parting of the sea, the whole exodus, all declared one thing: the Lord saves His people with power that no oppressor can resist.

And He did not stop at rescue. He brought them out, and then He brought them in — to a good land, flowing with milk and honey. Salvation is never just being taken out of something bad; it is being brought into something good.

This is the shape of the gospel. God saw us enslaved to sin, unable to free ourselves, and He acted. With the mighty hand of the cross and the outstretched arms of His Son, He rescued us (Col 1:13). He did not leave us wandering. He brought us out of darkness and into His kingdom, and He is bringing us home to a better land still.

We should be careful, though, not to read "milk and honey" as a promise of earthly wealth for us today. God's gift here was a specific land to a specific nation. The lasting principle is greater: our rescuing God brings His people into fullness of life with Him, secured forever in Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I marvel at the power of God that rescued me?
2. Am I living as someone God brought "out" and "into" His good purposes?
3. How does the cross show me God's mighty, saving hand?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Mighty God, You did not just pity me — You rescued me. Thank You for bringing me out of bondage and into life with You through Christ. I praise You for Your saving power. Amen.
